name: Mamelodi Sundowns 2025 (Miguel Cardoso)
scopeNote: Calendar year 2025 chosen by the user: second half of 2024/25 (Premiership, Nedbank Cup, CAF CL final lost to Pyramids), 2025 FIFA Club World Cup (17-25 June), first half of 2025/26. Club's own label is 'shoeshine and piano' (possession-based, one-touch). Sources describe a 4-2-3-1 base that becomes a back three in build-up (Mokoena dropping), a 4-1-4-1 out of possession, zonal marking at set pieces. Critics label it 'defensive' or 'like Stellenbosch'; Cardoso rejects this. Fact dates given as month/season where the day was not confirmed. Photo of 2025/26 league tactics is thin.
openQuestions: Mozzart Sport tactical piece on a Sundowns 3-1 win over RB Leipzig (4-4-2 mid-block, 5-2 build-up shape, aggressive high press in second half) is dated 2026-05-30, outside the period, so not recorded as evidence; useful for a later period.
Pressing triggers and open-play marking scheme (zonal vs man) in 2025 are not described by any tier A-B source found; only set-piece zonal marking is documented.
Dates given at month or year level for the CAF final legs and some press-conference facts; Maniema match day not confirmed.

statedView.quote: Dortmund play a very high tempo, aggressive style, which is typical of German football
The belief that African clubs lack organisation, especially when defending, is untrue
In the beginning, people were saying, 'Ah, maybe coach Miguel's style is not exactly Sundowns' style'. That's absolutely wrong
[in Portugal] People like some more objectivity or direct game, or speed. They don't like being under pressure in the build-up and still try to do it. And I was this kind of coach there.
You can have possession against them, but they always find a way to aggress you [...] we knew that we had to play our style. It was by imposing our style that we could create our moments.
Despite people saying, you coach, you are defensive. That's bullsh*t. [...] it's not true, we wanted to bring that energy to win the match.
